text:
jonah: heads up — saw a config "storm" last night when we bumped route-quota weights. consoles spammed coordinator and routers threw transient 503s. anyone have immediate theories? @oncall :wave:

alex: saw it too. apply-queue length jumped ~12k for ~90s. looks like every console save triggered immediate fanout to all routers.

maria: yep. current flow is console -> config-coordinator -> publish to all router shards (fanout). no debounce or coalescing. if two saves happen close, both get sent.

jonah: proposal: add per-key coalescing + short debounce (e.g., 100-300ms + jitter) in coordinator, and a best-effort merge for non-conflicting fields. reduces burst without affecting canary latency.

alex: +1 for debounce. question: how do we handle TTL/rollforward semantics? if we delay apply by 200ms, console UX might show slightly delayed effect. acceptable?

anya: for most flags a 200ms delay is fine. only a few ops flows need immediate effect (deadman switches, quota emergency pause). we should support bypass header for critical keys.

maria: implementation sketch:
```go
// pseudo
func scheduleApply(key, payload) {
  slot := slotsForKey(key)
  slot.mu.Lock()
  slot.pending = merge(slot.pending, payload)
  if !slot.timerActive {
    slot.timer = time.AfterFunc(debounce + jitter(), func() { flush(slot) })
    slot.timerActive = true
  }
  slot.mu.Unlock()
}
```
merge() would do field-level merge when safe, or mark conflict and force serial applies.

sam: curious how this plays with audit/ETag model. we still want deterministic ordering for history. coalescing shouldn't collapse separate user saves in audit log. can we emit an audit entry per incoming save even if we coalesce network applies?

maria: yes — keep auditable events at coordinator ingress. the coalesce only affects outbound publish to routers. audit log stays one-per-save with original payload.

taylor: telemetry asks: add metric for "coalesced_applies" and "apply_delay_ms" so we can monitor hidden latency. also expose sample of merged payloads for debugging.

jonah: good call. also throttling fallback: if coordinator queue grows > X, fall back to synchronous apply (or escalate to an emergency circuit) instead of trying to coalesce infinitely.

alex: one more: console preview. Console currently shows live effective config immediately after save because it reads coordinator state. with debounce, console should still read pending merge state so UX remains consistent. we may need a separate read path: /v1/config?preview=true -> reads pending merges.

anya: for critical keys we add header x-config-priority: urgent which bypasses debounce and forces immediate publish. ops playbook will document which keys are allowed.

sre-bot: incident note: 2025-07-12 23:18 UTC — transient 503 spike during quota-weight rollout. followups: implement coordinator-side debounce, add metrics, document bypass header.

jonah: next steps: maria to prototype coalescer + merge logic (start with safe atomic maps), alex to update console to read preview state, taylor to add telemetry and dashboards. aim for dry-run in staging next week.

maria: starting a small spike branch now, will ping this thread with a test plan and perf numbers. :thumbsup:

sam: quick test idea: sim 10k saves/sec on staging, measure peak apply rate to routers and audit write rates.

jonah: perfect. thanks all — appreciate the quick alignment. :rocket:
